title: Global Risks Heating Up
gist: This biweekly briefing is framed as covering China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and jihadists, but the accessible text is truncated by a members-only paywall after the Iran section only. That section reports the April US-Iran ceasefire and June 17 memorandum of understanding collapsing into near-daily hostilities, Trump declaring the ceasefire over on July 10, a resumed US naval blockade with daily strikes on Iranian soil, Iranian attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping and Arab Gulf states, three US soldiers killed in Jordan on July 17, and Trump signaling possible strikes on the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility plus bridges and power plants.

insights.claim: The US-Iranian ceasefire agreed in April and the memorandum of understanding signed on June 17 both deteriorated into near-constant exchange of hostilities by early July, with President Donald Trump declaring the ceasefire over on July 10.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Two failed de-escalation agreements in three months means the market should price diplomatic off-ramps in the Gulf as low-probability rather than base case.
insights.quote: On July 10, Trump declared that the ceasefire was over.

insights.claim: The United States has resumed a naval blockade of Iran and has been striking Iranian soil on a daily basis, in a conflict that began nearly five months ago.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: A sustained naval blockade plus daily strikes is a structurally different risk regime from episodic exchanges — it implies persistent tanker insurance, freight and crude supply disruption rather than headline spikes.
insights.quote: The United States resumed its naval blockade and has been striking Iranian soil on a daily basis.

insights.claim: Iran has targeted vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz while launching drones and missiles at Arab Gulf states and further west into Jordan and Syria, killing three US soldiers in Jordan on July 17.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Direct attacks on Hormuz shipping plus US fatalities on Jordanian soil are the two escalation markers most likely to force a larger US response and a crude risk premium.
insights.locator: Iran has targeted vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz

insights.claim: Trump has indicated the United States may soon target Pickaxe Mountain, a facility where Israeli intelligence reportedly believes Iran might be holding advanced centrifuges and some enriched uranium.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: A named hardened nuclear target signals a possible step-change in the campaign; strikes on enrichment infrastructure historically trigger the largest Iranian retaliation and energy-market reaction.

insights.claim: Growing indications of intensifying hostilities include reported movements of US forces and warnings from Trump that the United States might expand its target set to include bridges and power plants.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Expansion from military to civilian-adjacent infrastructure targets would mark a shift toward a coercive-pressure campaign, raising the odds of prolonged Iranian energy-sector retaliation.
insights.locator: In recent days and hours, there have been growing indications

insights.claim: Mediation is failing because both Washington and Tehran, having earlier come to the table to break a lose-lose dynamic of mounting economic and military costs, have each reverted to a belief that escalation might yield a better return.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: The stated mechanism — both sides now expect escalation to pay — means the conflict likely intensifies before any truce; only rising costs, not diplomacy, will reverse it.
insights.quote: each seems to have reverted to a belief that escalation might yield a better return
insights.locator: Mediators are trying to secure another truce

insights.claim: Both sides are divided internally on the necessity and substance of an off-ramp and deeply mistrustful of the other's objectives, making continuation and potential intensification the base case for a conflict that has already run through several cycles of fighting and diplomacy.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Internal division on both sides means even a negotiated pause would be fragile — assume repeated ceasefire-and-collapse cycles rather than resolution when sizing Gulf risk exposure.
insights.locator: Divided on both the necessity and substance of an off-ramp
